title: dsamoht/roshab-cli pipeline parameters
description: Microbiome taxonomic classification and evaluation of cyanotoxin biosynthesis potential from nanopore reads

input_output_options.title: Input/output options
input_output_options.description: Define where the pipeline should find input data and save output data.

input.description: Path to comma-separated file containing information about the samples in the experiment.
input.help_text: You will need to create a design file with information about the samples in your experiment before running the pipeline. Use this parameter to specify its location. It has to be a comma-separated file with 5 columns: `sample_id`, `group`, `info`, `date` and `reads`.

outdir.description: The output directory where the results will be saved. You have to use absolute paths to storage on Cloud infrastructure.

email.help_text: Set this parameter to your e-mail address to get a summary e-mail with details of the run sent to you when the workflow exits. If set in your user config file (`~/.nextflow/config`) then you don't need to specify this on the command line for every run.

multiqc_title.description: MultiQC report title. Printed as page header, used for filename if not otherwise specified.

reference_databases.title: Reference databases
reference_databases.description: Databases used by the taxonomic profiling and cyanotoxin screening steps.
reference_databases.help_text: None of these databases are downloaded by the pipeline. Directories and `.tar.gz`/`.tgz` tarballs are both accepted for the database parameters that point at a directory: tarballs are extracted once at the start of the run.

kraken_db.description: Path to a Kraken2 database (directory or `.tar.gz` tarball).
kraken_db.help_text: Pre-built indexes are available from https://benlangmead.github.io/aws-indexes/k2. The database must contain `ktaxonomy.tsv`, which is used to rebuild the per-sample Kraken2 reports.

genomes_db.description: Path to the genome database used by CoverM (directory of FASTA files or `.tar.gz` tarball).
genomes_db.help_text: The reference set used during development is available at https://zenodo.org/records/19522349/files/cyanobacteriota_ncbi_dRep_n220.tar.gz

genes_db.description: Path to the FASTA file of cyanotoxin-related protein sequences used by DIAMOND.

antismash_db.description: Path to the antiSMASH databases (directory or `.tar.gz` tarball). Required with `--mode assembly` or `--mode both`.
antismash_db.help_text: Create with `download-antismash-databases` from the antiSMASH distribution.

deepbgc_db.description: Path to the DeepBGC models (directory or `.tar.gz` tarball). Required with `--run_deepbgc`.

database_installation.title: Database installation
database_installation.description: Download the reference databases instead of running an analysis.
database_installation.help_text: Setting `--db_dir` switches the run to database installation: the requested databases are downloaded into that directory, one directory per database, and no analysis step runs. Databases that are already present are skipped, so an interrupted install can simply be re-run.

db_dir.description: Directory to install the reference databases into. Setting it runs the database installation and nothing else.
db_dir.help_text: Each database is installed into its own subdirectory: `kraken_db`, `genomes_db`, `genes_db`, `antismash_db`, `deepbgc_db` and `pfam_db`. The install run prints the parameter values to use afterwards.

install_databases.description: Which databases to install with `--db_dir`: `all`, or a comma-separated list of `kraken`, `genomes`, `genes`, `antismash`, `deepbgc`, `pfam`.

kraken_db_url.help_text: The default is the 16 GB capped PlusPF index. Any other index from https://benlangmead.github.io/aws-indexes/k2 can be used instead, as long as it contains `ktaxonomy.tsv`.

pfam_db_url.description: Pfam-A HMM profiles downloaded by `--db_dir`, used by BiG-SCAPE.

workflow_options.title: Workflow options
workflow_options.description: Select which cyanotoxin screening route to run.

mode.help_text: `reads` runs `diamond blastx` on the QC reads (minutes). `assembly` assembles the reads and screens the contigs for biosynthetic gene clusters (hours, high memory). `both` runs the two routes on the same reads. Taxonomic profiling runs in every mode.

skip_qc.description: Skip the read QC steps (NanoPlot and Chopper).

skip_nanoplot.description: Skip the NanoPlot quality assessment but still run Chopper.

chopper_headcrop.description: Number of bases to trim from the start of each read.

chopper_tailcrop.description: Number of bases to trim from the end of each read.

chopper_minlength.description: Minimum read length to keep after trimming.

chopper_minq.description: Minimum average read quality to keep.

kraken_confidence.description: Kraken2 confidence score threshold, between 0 and 1.
kraken_confidence.help_text: Fraction of a read's k-mers that must map to a taxon's clade for the read to be assigned to it. `0` (the default) keeps Kraken2's own default behaviour; higher values make classification more conservative at the cost of sensitivity.

bracken_length.description: Read length Bracken was built for, also used as the SeqKit sliding window and step size.
bracken_length.help_text: Long reads are segmented into non-overlapping windows of this length before Kraken2 classification so that the read lengths match the Bracken k-mer distribution.

read_screening_options.title: Read-level screening options
read_screening_options.description: Options for the `--mode reads` DIAMOND screening route.

diamond_blastx_id.description: Minimum percentage identity of the read-level `diamond blastx` alignments.

assembly_options.title: Assembly options
assembly_options.description: Options for the `--mode assembly` / `--mode both` assembly steps.

assembler.description: Assembler used for the contig-level route.

assembly_cpus.description: CPUs given to the assembly and antiSMASH steps. Overrides the `process_high` default.
assembly_cpus.help_text: Memory and time still come from the `process_high` label, so set them in a custom config (`-c my.config`) when running on a scheduler.

coassemble_by_group.description: Co-assemble all the samples of a group instead of producing one assembly per sample.

min_contig_length.description: Minimum contig length kept for screening, also passed to antiSMASH as `--minlength`.

bgc_screening_options.title: BGC screening options
bgc_screening_options.description: Options for the biosynthetic gene cluster detection steps.

diamond_blastp_id.description: Minimum percentage identity of the contig-level `diamond blastp` alignments.

bgc_min_overlap.description: Overlap (bp) at which two tools are considered to call the same BGC region.
bgc_min_overlap.help_text: Regions supported by at least two tools after merging are labelled `high` confidence in the per-sample `*.bgc.tsv` table.

run_deepbgc.description: Add DeepBGC to the antiSMASH + GECCO screening. Requires `--deepbgc_db`.

run_bigscape.description: Cluster the antiSMASH regions into gene cluster families per group. Requires `--pfam_db`.

institutional_config_options.title: Institutional config options
institutional_config_options.description: Parameters used to describe centralised config profiles. These should not be edited.
institutional_config_options.help_text: The centralised nf-core configuration profiles use a handful of pipeline parameters to describe themselves. This information is then printed to the Nextflow log when you run a pipeline. You should not need to change these values when you run a pipeline.

custom_config_version.description: Git commit id for Institutional configs.

custom_config_base.help_text: If you're running offline, Nextflow will not be able to fetch the institutional config files from the internet. If you don't need them, then this is not a problem. If you do need them, you should download the files from the repo and tell Nextflow where to find them with this parameter.

generic_options.title: Generic options
generic_options.description: Less common options for the pipeline, typically set in a config file.
generic_options.help_text: These options are common to all nf-core pipelines and allow you to customise some of the core preferences for pipeline execution.

publish_dir_mode.description: Method used to save pipeline results to output directory.
publish_dir_mode.help_text: The Nextflow `publishDir` option specifies which intermediate files should be saved to the output directory. This option tells the pipeline what method should be used to move these files. See [Nextflow docs](https://www.nextflow.io/docs/latest/process.html#publishdir) for details.

email_on_fail.description: Email address for completion summary, only when pipeline fails.
email_on_fail.help_text: An email address to send a summary email to when the pipeline is completed - ONLY sent if the pipeline does not exit successfully.

plaintext_email.description: Send plain-text email instead of HTML.

max_multiqc_email_size.description: File size limit when attaching MultiQC reports to summary emails.

monochrome_logs.description: Do not use coloured log outputs.

multiqc_config.description: Custom config file to supply to MultiQC.

multiqc_logo.description: Custom logo file to supply to MultiQC. File name must also be set in the MultiQC config file.

multiqc_methods_description.description: Custom MultiQC yaml file containing HTML including a methods description.

validate_params.description: Boolean whether to validate parameters against the schema at runtime.

pipelines_testdata_base_path.description: Base URL or local path to location of pipeline test dataset files.

trace_report_suffix.description: Suffix to add to the trace report filename. Default is the date and time in the format yyyy-MM-dd_HH-mm-ss.

help_full.description: Display the full help text, including hidden parameters.
